summary: Iteration-6: Verified Orb voice-chat backend pipeline + frontend regression after Orb.jsx fixes. Backend 5/5 passed (chat→Anthropic claude-sonnet-4-6 returns non-empty reply + conversation_id; voice/tts returns audio/mpeg with valid MP3 magic ~24KB; voice/transcribe route exists and responds with sane non-404 status; auth gating enforced on /api/chat; bad-password rejected). Frontend SPA loads on / (redirects to /login passkey screen) and /install with ZERO page errors and ZERO console errors. Code review of Orb.jsx confirmed all 3 fixes are in place.
critical_code_review_comments: Orb.jsx speak() (lines 157-194): returns boolean (true on audio playback success, false on TTS failure). On catch, classifies 401/503 as 'Voice is unavailable (check your ElevenLabs API key).' and otherwise 'Voice playback failed.' — toast.error surfaces the spoken text as description (sliced 180 chars) so the user STILL sees the assistant reply even when ElevenLabs is broken. Exactly what was requested.

Orb.jsx ask() (lines 196-220): catch block now reads e?.response?.data?.detail || e?.message and calls toast.error('Promethius couldn't respond', { description: msg }). Additionally, if speak() returned false but reply text exists, a secondary toast() surfaces the reply (240 chars). The previous silent swallow is fully gone. Confirmed.

Orb.jsx handleFinal() (lines 294-319): wake-word detection switched from lastIndexOf('promethius') to text.match(/prom[ae]th[a-z]*/) — correctly matches 'prometheus', 'promethease', 'promathius' etc. Index + length are then used to slice the trailing query. Confirmed.

MINOR (pre-existing, not in scope): forget() catch still has bare '// ignore' (line 259). Not a regression — wasn't part of this fix — but the same anti-pattern that caused the original bug lives on for the enroll/forget commands.

Backend /api/voice/tts gracefully falls back to OpenAI TTS if ElevenLabs raises (lines 776-781). Cloud test confirmed ElevenLabs path is hit (24KB MP3 with ID3/0xFF header). Local users with empty ELEVENLABS_API_KEY will hit the OpenAI fallback — but their OpenAI key is OUT_OF_QUOTA per test_credentials.md, so they would 500. The new toast in speak() now correctly surfaces that to the user.
server.py still ~1390 lines, single module. Same long-standing recommendation: split into routers. Not blocking.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Six backend test suites: backend_test.py (regression), iteration2..5_test.py, iteration6_test.py (chat+tts+transcribe). All Orb.jsx voice/wake-word/error-surfacing fixes verified by code review — no UI testing of the orb itself is possible because it's behind a passkey login (WebAuthn cannot be exercised headlessly). The user's local 'no response' issue is now visible via toasts: if their local Anthropic key is empty they will see 'Promethius couldn't respond' with the actual server error; if their ElevenLabs key is empty they will see 'Voice is unavailable' plus the reply text as a toast. ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in /app/backend/.env are valid in the cloud preview.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE (in user's local env): Orb.ask() previously swallowed all errors silently ('// ignore'), so if their local ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was empty/invalid the chat call failed with 500 but produced no UI feedback — user heard nothing and assumed the mic was broken. Compounding: (a) speak() also swallowed TTS errors, so even if chat succeeded, an empty ElevenLabs key would silently kill the voice; (b) wake-word required exact 'promethius' substring, but Chrome's SpeechRecognition transcribes it as 'prometheus'/'promethease', so the user's voice never even reached ask(). FIX VERIFIED: (1) ask() catch surfaces toast.error with server detail; (2) speak() returns bool + toast.error on TTS failure with the reply text as description so the user still sees the answer; (3) handleFinal() uses /prom[ae]th[a-z]*/ regex. MITIGATION FOR USER: open the install guide, double-check ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in their local backend/.env, restart backend. The new toasts will now tell them exactly which key is bad.
